title: Stride offline-first sync rewrite
context: Stride is an open-source (MIT) running and workout tracker for iOS and Android (React Native, SQLite on device) with ~90,000 active users. Its README and project charter promise that users can self-host the sync server (a published Docker image used by ~3,000 self-hosted instances) and fully own their workout data. Current sync is a REST endpoint that breaks on poor connectivity. This plan is about to be dispatched to 3 contributors for a 5-week build.
artifact:
# Offline-first sync — build plan

Maintainers: core team | 5 weeks | Ships in app 4.0

## 1. Problem
- 23% of sync-related GitHub issues in the last 6 months are "workout lost/duplicated after trail run with no signal".
- Current REST sync uploads whole-workout blobs; a dropped connection mid-upload leaves a partial server row and a client that believes the upload failed, which then re-uploads a duplicate.

## 2. Approach
Adopt Cirrus Sync, a mobile offline-first sync SDK:
- Local writes go to an on-device Cirrus store; Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud when connectivity returns.
- Per-record change tracking; uploads are resumable at the record level, so a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout.
- Pricing: free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier.
- The Cirrus client SDK is distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license; the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service.

## 3. Self-hosted instances
Self-hosted servers keep working through the transition: app 4.x continues to speak the legacy REST sync protocol when the user has configured a custom server URL. Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0 (planned for end of next year), after which Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived.

## 4. Conflict resolution
- Workouts are append-only after the "finish" event; edits after finish (title, notes, gear) are per-field last-writer-wins using a hybrid logical clock stamped on device.
- Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout.
- Unit tests cover the 14 conflict scenarios enumerated in docs/sync-conflicts.md.

## 5. On-device migration
- On first launch of 4.0, the app copies the existing SQLite database to stride-backup-v3.db before migrating into the Cirrus store.
- If migration fails or the user downgrades to 3.x, 3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it; the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs.
- Migration is chunked (500 workouts per batch) and resumable if the app is killed mid-migration.

## 6. Timeline
- Week 1: Cirrus integration spike, schema mapping (workouts, laps, GPS tracks, gear).
- Week 2: on-device migration + backup/restore path.
- Week 3: conflict resolution + tests; legacy REST path behind custom-server flag.
- Week 4: beta (TestFlight / Play internal) to 500 volunteers, including 50 trail runners.
- Week 5: staged rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%, halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%.

## 7. Data export and deletion
- Settings > Export keeps working unchanged: GPX per workout and a full JSON archive, generated on device from the local store.
- Account deletion removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days.

## 8. Success metrics
- "Lost/duplicated workout" issues down 80% within 2 months of 4.0.
- Sync success rate (client-reported) >= 99.5% on beta cohort.

defects.description: The plan makes a closed-source, hosted-only vendor service the single sync backend and schedules archiving the self-hostable server, breaking the project's charter promise that users can self-host and own their data. It also creates a single-provider dependency whose free tier (100k devices) the app is already at 90% of. Needs a self-hostable sync design (or an open-source sync engine) instead.
defects.evidence: after which Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived

decoys: Irreversible on-device schema migration / downgrade breakage: handled in §5 — pre-migration backup, 3.x restore path on downgrade, resumable chunked migration, delayed backup deletion.
Offline edit conflicts and resurrected deletes: handled in §4 — append-only workouts, per-field HLC last-writer-wins, 90-day tombstones, enumerated conflict tests.
